title: "Spine Text Not Allowed" on a Thin Book: How to Fix It (KDP & IngramSpark) | SparkPrep
h1: How to fix "spine text not allowed" on a thin book
description: Your cover was rejected because your book is too thin for spine text. See the page counts KDP and IngramSpark require and how to fix your cover fast.
lead: Thin books have thin spines, and printers won't print words on a spine that's too narrow to hold them.
error: Spine text is not allowed for books under the minimum page count
errorNote: Paraphrased. Each printer words this a little differently.
why:
A spine is only as wide as your pages are thick. On a thin book, the spine might be a few millimeters wide. The printer's fold can shift a tiny bit, so words on a very thin spine can wrap onto the front or back cover.

That's why printers set a minimum: Amazon KDP only allows spine text on books with more than 79 pages, and IngramSpark doesn't allow spine text on paperbacks under 48 pages. If your book is under the line and the spine has words on it, the cover is rejected.
manual: Check your final page count against the rule: more than 79 pages for KDP, at least 48 for IngramSpark paperbacks.
If you're under it, delete the title, author name and any logo from the spine. Keep just the background color or art there.
Re-export as PDF/X-1a:2001 with the bleed included.
Re-upload it to your printer and wait for the file review again. If it fails, you start over.

cta.text: Not sure if your book is thick enough for spine text? SparkPrep checks your page count against your printer's rule and tells you before you upload.

faq.q: How many pages do you need for spine text on KDP?
faq.a: Amazon KDP allows spine text only on books with more than 79 pages.

faq.q: How many pages do you need for spine text on IngramSpark?
faq.a: IngramSpark doesn't allow spine text on paperback covers under 48 pages.
